docs.title: Cache (dox_cache)
docs.text:
dox_cache is a cache like Laravel Cache. It has remember, tags, atomic locks and four drivers.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_cache for Cache(). In a Dox app, set the stores in config/cache.dart (the CacheConfig of this page), and use Cache(). Dox().cache is the CacheManager. Cache().repository is the CacheStore. This page is for the full API and for using dox_cache outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_cache

import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

Note

dox_core exports CacheConfig, CacheManager, CacheStore and CacheLock from this package. They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Driver What it is Shared between isolates memory a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit No file one JSON file per key in a folder Yes (same machine) redis Redis, with the ioredis package Yes null stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off -

Warning

Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own memory cache. Use redis when isolates or servers must see the same data.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store

Redis options: host, port, username, password, db, tls, prefix.

docs.title: Basic use
docs.text:
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');

No ttl means forever

put without a ttl keeps the value forever. (The old Cache() in dox_core keeps it for 1 hour.) A zero or negative ttl removes the key.

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});

docs.title: All methods
docs.text: Method What it does get(key, [default]) the value, or the default when missing or expired put(key, value, [ttl]) store it add(key, value, [ttl]) store only when missing. Returns true when stored has(key) true when the value is not null forget(key) remove it. Returns true when it was there flush() remove all items of this store many(keys) / putMany(map, [ttl]) many keys at once increment(key, [by]) / decrement(key, [by]) change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays forever(key, value) store without expiry remember(key, ttl, compute) see above rememberForever(key, compute) the same, without expiry pull(key) get it, then remove it tags([...]) a tagged view lock(name, [ttl]) an atomic lock

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text:
Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool, null. Other types throw.

  • A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>. A List comes back as List<dynamic>.
  • A stored null reads as a miss. has returns false for it.
  • For a model, store model.toJson(), not the model.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Only one worker runs the code at a time.

CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds

memory and redis support locks. The memory lock works inside one isolate only.

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
Every store has a prefix (default dox_cache:). It is added to every key. Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database.

Redis flush

flush deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs FLUSHDB. An empty prefix makes flush throw.

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver

MyDriver extends CacheDriver and implements get, put, add, increment, forget and flush.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text:
Dox makes OpenAPI 3.1 docs for your API by itself. You write no docs code. You get a Scalar docs page at /docs, plus /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml.

The docs come from three places:

  • the routes: method, path, path params, middleware (login),
  • the request classes: a @Dto class,
  • the controllers: the /// comment, the arguments and the return type of each method.

docs.title: 1. Run the builder
docs.text:
dart run build_runner build      # or: dox build_runner:build

dox_builder reads your code and writes lib/openapi.g.dart. Run it again after you change routes, controllers, request classes or models. dox build_runner:watch does it for you while you work.

docs.title: 2. Pass the result to the config
docs.text:
// lib/config/openapi.dart
import 'package:my_app/openapi.g.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);

AppConfig(openApi: openApi, ...);

docs.title: 3. Open /docs
docs.text:
Start the app and open http://localhost:3000/docs.

  • enabled is null by default. The docs are on only when APP_ENV is development or local. So production is off unless you set enabled: true.
  • When the docs are off, there is no extra work per request.
  • The document is built and encoded on the first /docs request, then kept. It is built again only when routes are added.

docs.title: The docs page
docs.text:
/docs uses Scalar by default. The page loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN, at a fixed version, and reads /openapi.json.

Change the look with scalar::

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',          // default: info.title
  scalar: ScalarOptions(
    theme: ScalarTheme.purple,         // default: ScalarTheme.default_
    darkMode: true,                    // start in dark mode (default: false)
    showDownloadButton: false,         // hide "Download OpenAPI" (default: true)
    proxyUrl: 'https://proxy.scalar.com', // default: null, no proxy
  ),
);
Option Default What it does theme ScalarTheme.default_ Color theme. Same names as Scalar: moon, purple, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, mars and more. darkMode false Start in dark mode. The user can still switch. showDownloadButton true Show the button that downloads the document. proxyUrl null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Off by default, so requests go from the browser straight to your API.

pageTitle and all options are escaped, so a value can not break the page.

To use Swagger UI instead, set ui::

OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);

docs.title: What you write, what you get
docs.text:
A normal controller. There are no docs annotations here:

class BlogController {
  /// Get one blog
  ///
  /// Deleted blogs are not found.
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }

  /// Create a blog
  Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body) async { ... }
}

// routes
Route.get('/blogs/{id}', [AuthMiddleware(), blogController.show]);

The generated docs for GET /blogs/{id}:

get:
  tags: [Blog]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []

Blog is in components/schemas, made from the model:

Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}

docs.title: How each part is found
docs.text:
Part of the docs Where it comes from path, method the live route table path param types the controller arguments after the first one, in order. int id gives integer tags the controller class name without Controller (BlogController gives Blog) operationId Class.method, for example BlogController.show summary the first line of the /// comment description the rest of the /// comment request see Request below 200 answer the return type, see Response below 401 and bearerAuth a middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware 404 the path has a {param} 422 the route has a request class. The body is {field: message} 500 every route

Routes that the builder does not know (for example inline closures) still get a basic entry.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
The builder looks in this order. The first one wins.

  1. @Body(T), @Query(T) or @Request(T) on the method.
  2. An argument whose type is a @Dto class: store(CreateBlog body).
  3. A req.validate<T>() call in the method, where T is a @Dto class.

For POST, PUT and PATCH the request is the JSON body. For other methods each field is one query parameter. @Dto(source: Source.query) or Source.body chooses the place by hand. The route body: option still works, and it wins over all of these.

A @Dto class:

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}

The keys are the same as the keys the DTO reads: snake_case by default (postCode is post_code), or @Name('key'), or @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field). Each rule annotation adds its JSON Schema keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The return type of the method gives the 200 answer. Future<T> counts as T.

Return type Schema a model (@DoxModel) $ref to the model. Keys in hidden are left out List<Model> an array of the model a @Dto class $ref to the class a Serializer<Model> the map that convert() returns, else the model Pagination total, per_page, last_page, current_page, data String, int, bool, Map, List the basic JSON type dynamic the types of the return values. A map literal gives its keys. Exceptions are left out DoxResponse, void no schema

A model schema has the primary key, the @Column fields, created_at, updated_at, the relations (only there when loaded) and the @Computed getters.

docs.title: Change the docs (optional)
docs.text:
Add these to a controller method when the automatic result is not what you want. They are all in dox_core.

@Summary('Log in')
@Description('Gives a bearer token for the Authorization header.')
@Tags(<String>['Auth'])
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
Annotation What it does @Summary('text') short title. Default: the first line of the /// comment @Description('text') longer text. Default: the rest of the /// comment @Tags(['Users']) groups. On a method or on the class @Request(T) the request class. Body or query by the HTTP method @Body(T) the request class, always the body @Query(T) the request class, always the query @Response(status, Type, description: '') one answer. Add more than one for more codes. With a 2xx one, the return type is not used @ApiDeprecated() marks the route as deprecated. Dart @Deprecated works too @ApiIgnore() leaves the method (or the whole class) out of the docs @DoxController(tag: 'Users') for a class that the builder can not see in a Route.get(...) call

The Type of @Response can be a model, List<User>, a @Dto, a Serializer or a basic type like String.

Lower case names work too: @summary('Log in'), @description(...), @tags(...), @request(...), @body(...), @query(...), @apiDeprecated(), @apiIgnore(), @doxController(). The capital form is the normal Dart style. @Response has no lower case name, because response() is already the response helper of dox_core.

docs.title: Login schemes
docs.text:
A middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware adds bearerAuth (a JWT bearer token) by itself. For other middleware, or another scheme, set it in the config:

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'X-API-Key'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);

docs.title: How a route finds its docs
docs.text:
Routes are added when the app starts, so the builder can not see the final route table. It writes two lists into openapi.g.dart:

  • the docs of each controller method, by Class.method,
  • each Route.get(...) / Route.resource(...) call it found, with its path and Class.method.

At runtime, Dox reads the method name of each route handler. It picks the route call with the same HTTP method and the same end of path. If there is none, it picks the only method with that name and the same argument types. Group prefixes (like api/) do not matter.

Tip

If two controllers have a method with the same name, register the routes with Route.get('path', controller.method) so the builder can see them.

docs.title: Write the files: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder

It runs bin/openapi.dart of your app:

// bin/openapi.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}

writeOpenApi runs your services and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_openapi also works on its own. Describe routes by hand with ApiDoc:

import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // returns a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);

api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // body + content type for /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /docs
// Swagger UI: OpenApiServer(api, ui: DocsUi.swagger)

A schema can be a JSON Schema Map, a dox_validation schema, or any object with toJsonSchema(). Paths can use {id} or :id. Both become {id}. DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes) adds a basic entry for each route you did not describe.

Tip

Do not serve /docs in production if your API is private.

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
dox_socketio is a Socket.IO server for Dart. The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package.

Socket.IO or WebSocket?

  • WebSocket (dox_websocket) runs inside the Dox HTTP server. It uses its own small JSON format.
  • Socket.IO (this page) works with the Socket.IO clients. It has acks, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.on('connection', onConnection);
  await io.listen(3001);
}

void onConnection(Socket socket) {
  socket.emit('welcome', 'hello');
  socket.join('lobby');
  socket.on('chat', onChat);
}

void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
  event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
  event.ack('ok'); // answer the client callback
}

Client (JavaScript):

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3001');
socket.emit('chat', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'ok'

docs.title: In a Dox app: same port as HTTP
docs.text:
dox_core can serve Socket.IO at /socket.io/ on the app port. It is off by default.

// config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIo = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false),
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(), // shares broadcasts between isolates
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

AppConfig(socketIo: socketIo, ...);
  • Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped.
  • When it is off, there is no extra work per request.
  • Dox().socketIo is the server of this isolate: Dox().socketIo?.to('room').emit('news', data).
  • dox_websocket (Route.websocket) still works next to it.

Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server.

  • Clients should connect with websocket only. One websocket stays on one isolate. With the Redis adapter, a broadcast reaches clients on every isolate.
  • HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates. It only works with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.
const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });

Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

docs.title: Where to run it (outside Dox)
docs.text:
io.listen(port) opens its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example bin/socket.dart, next to the Dox HTTP server. Put both behind the same proxy.

  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a dart:io server you already have.
  • In your own dart:io server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • The path is /socket.io/ by default.

docs.title: Namespaces in a class
docs.text:
A namespace can be a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: {'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

io.register(ChatNamespace(MessageService()));

When a middleware throws, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data.

docs.title: Node.js to Dart
docs.text:
Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r) / socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address socket.data socket.data (a Map) io.in(r).fetchSockets() io.to(r).fetchSockets() (this server only)
  • disconnecting and disconnect give the reason in event.data, like transport close or ping timeout.
  • Binary data: send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: ['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: ['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
With more than one server process, use the Redis adapter. Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

Redis sub = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: sub, publisher: sub.duplicate()),
);
  • It uses the message format of @socket.io/redis-adapter. A Node.js server can share broadcasts with it, when Node uses a JSON parser.
  • fetchSockets, socketsJoin and broadcast acks only work on the local server.
  • Long-polling needs sticky sessions when many servers share one port. If you can not have them, use transports: ['websocket'] on the client.

docs.title: Storage (dox_storage)
docs.text:
dox_storage gives one API for files on many places: local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services. The API follows FlyDrive and Laravel Filesystem.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_storage for Storage(). In a Dox app, set the disks in config/storage.dart (a StorageConfig), and use Storage(). Storage().use('s3') gives the Disk of this page. Route.files('files') serves local signed URLs. This page is for the full Disk API and for using dox_storage outside Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_storage

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: Driver Use for Signed download URL Signed upload URL LocalDriver a folder on the server Yes (HMAC with your app key) No S3Driver AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) Yes (SigV4) Yes (SigV4) MemoryDriver tests fake URLs fake URLs

docs.title: Set up the disks
docs.text:
DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      appKey: Env.get('APP_KEY'),
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: Env.get('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID'),
      secretAccessKey: Env.get('AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'),
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk

docs.title: Use a disk
docs.text:
await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes); // String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');
String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');
Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');
ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png'); // size, contentType, lastModified, etag
bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');

await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');
await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');
await disk.delete('c.png');
await disk.deleteAll('avatars');

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);

docs.title: Save an upload
docs.text:
Stream the upload to the disk. The file is not loaded into memory.

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  await disk.putStream('avatars/${file.filename}', file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl('avatars/${file.filename}')};
});

Warning

Do not use the file name from the client as it is. Make your own name, for example with a uuid.

docs.title: URLs and signed URLs
docs.text:
String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

// a download link that works for 10 minutes
String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

// the browser can upload straight to S3 with this URL
String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));
  • S3 signed URLs can live at most 7 days. This is an S3 rule.
  • Set urlBase to serve public files from a CDN.

docs.title: Check a local signed URL
docs.text:
In a Dox app, Route.files('files') does this for you.

LocalDriver.getSignedUrl returns <urlBase>/<key>?expires=...&signature=.... Check it in the route that serves the file:

bool ok = local.verifySignedUrl(keyFromPath, req.uri.queryParameters);
if (!ok) {
  return response('Forbidden').statusCode(403);
}

docs.title: S3-compatible services
docs.text:
Cloudflare R2MinIODigitalOcean SpacesGoogle Cloud Storage 
S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
);

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'us-east-1',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
  accessKeyId: 'minioadmin',
  secretAccessKey: 'minioadmin',
);

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-space',
  region: 'nyc3',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
);

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
  accessKeyId: 'GOOG...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
  supportsBatchDelete: false,
);

Big files

  • put sends one request. S3 allows at most 5 GiB in one request.
  • putStream uses a multipart upload when the stream is bigger than multipartPartSize (8 MiB). Only one part is in memory at a time. The limit is about 78 GiB. Raise multipartPartSize for bigger files.
  • copy and move copy on the server. S3 allows at most 5 GiB here.

docs.title: Keys are checked
docs.text:
• a//b/./c.txt becomes a/b/c.txt. \ becomes /.
  • .., absolute paths (/etc/passwd) and null bytes throw InvalidKeyException.
  • LocalDriver also checks that the path stays inside its root folder.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors extend StorageException and have the key.

Error When FileNotFoundException the file does not exist PermissionDeniedException file system permission error, or S3 403 InvalidKeyException unsafe key UnsupportedOperationException the driver can not do this DriverException anything else. The first error is in cause

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
fake() swaps a disk for a memory disk.

Disk fake = drive.fake('s3'); // drive.use('s3') now writes to memory
await uploadAvatar();         // your code
expect(await fake.exists('avatars/1.png'), isTrue);
drive.restore('s3');

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
Implement DriverContract and register it.

class DropboxDriver implements DriverContract { ... }

drive.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver(...));
await drive.use('dropbox').put('a.txt', 'hello');

docs.title: dox_validation
docs.text:
dox_validation checks input and gives you typed Dart objects. It has two parts:

  1. DTOs: a class with @Dto() and rule annotations. A generator writes the checks. Use this for almost everything.
  2. Fluent schemas: v.object(...), like Zod. Use it only when the shape is known at runtime.

Both give all errors at once, and a JSON Schema for OpenAPI.

Built into Dox

dox_core uses dox_validation and exports it. import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' is all you need. The guide is at Validation. Every rule is in the rules reference. This page is about the package itself, and about using it outside Dox.

docs.title: Install (outside Dox)
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

The DTO generator is in dox_builder. Run it with dart run build_runner build. @Unique and @Exists are in dox_orm, not here.

docs.title: DTOs
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

The generator makes, for each @Dto class:

Name What it is $CreateUserDto a const DtoSchema<CreateUser>: the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema lib/dtos.g.dart const List<DtoSchema<Object>> dtos: every DTO in lib/. Dox uses it to find DTOs by type.

The static const ... schema = $CreateUserDto; line is how you reach the schema: CreateUser.schema.

docs.title: DtoSchema<T>
docs.text:
DtoSchema<T> is also a Schema<T>. So it works everywhere a schema works: inside v.object(...), v.list(...), with OpenAPI, and as a StandardSchema.

Member Does Future<T> validateMap(Map<String, dynamic> input, {Source source = Source.body, Map<String, String> params = const {}}) all checks, then the object. Throws ValidationException with the errors. Future<ParseResult<T>> safeValidateMap(input, {source, params}) the same, but never throws for bad input. result.success, result.value, result.errors. T fromMap(Map<String, dynamic> input) builds the object with no checks. Reads keys, converts JSON types, uses defaults. A wrong type throws a TypeError. Only for data you trust. Map<String, dynamic> toMap(T value) the object as a map with the input keys (snake_case). DateTime becomes an ISO 8601 string, an enum its name. Map<String, dynamic> toJsonSchema() JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). parse, safeParse, parseAsync, safeParseAsync the normal Schema methods, with Source.body. parse throws a StateError when the DTO has async rules. Type get type, String get name CreateUser and 'CreateUser'.

source: Source.query reads the map like a query string: text is converted to the field type. params are path params, used by @Unique(ignoreParam: ...).

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}

Note

dox_core has its own ValidationException (the HTTP 422 one), so it does not export the one from dox_validation. In a Dox app, both answer 422 when thrown in a controller. In tests, prefer safeValidateMap.

docs.title: JSON Schema of a DTO
docs.text:
For the CreateUser from the Validation guide (with age and role):

CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}
  • required lists the required fields only.
  • A nullable field has "type": [..., "null"]. A default becomes default.
  • A nested DTO goes in $defs under its class name, with a $ref. OpenAPI moves it to components/schemas.
  • @Dto(strict: true) adds "additionalProperties": false.
  • A /// doc comment on a field becomes description.
  • Each rule adds its keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)
docs.text:
Use these when you only know the fields at runtime. The output is a Map, not a class.

final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

// throws ValidationException when the input is not valid
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

// never throws for bad input
ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);

In a controller: Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);

Different defaults

Fluent schemas do not follow the DTO rules. A key is required unless you add optional(). "" is a value, not "missing". Text is not converted, unless you use v.coerce.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has image and extensions

On every schema:

  • optional(): the key may be missing. null is still an error.
  • nullable(): the value may be null. The key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing. (default is a reserved word in Dart.)
  • transform(fn), refine(fn), refineAsync(fn), superRefine(fn), use(rule).
  • describe(text), example(x): only used in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Coercion
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are text. v.coerce turns text into the right type first.

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checks across fields
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text: refineAsync runs a check that needs the database. Then use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync(). parse() throws a StateError when a schema has async checks.

docs.title: Custom rules in a fluent schema
docs.text:
A Rule<T> class works in both worlds: as an annotation on a DTO, and with use() here.

v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());

See Custom rules for how to write one.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. Placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

// for the whole app (outside Dox; in Dox use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...))
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

// for one call
createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve(). See Messages.

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.text: Every schema, and every DtoSchema, implements the Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema). Code that only needs to validate can accept any StandardSchema, from Dox or from another library.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
YAMLCLI 
dependencies:
...
dox_auth: <latest>

dart pub add dox_auth

Package link : https://pub.dev/packages/dox_auth

docs.title: 1. Setup auth service
docs.text:
Create auth service file lib/services/auth_service.dart.

class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(
      /// default auth guard
      defaultGuard: 'web',

      /// list of auth guards
      guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
        'web': AuthGuard(
          driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(Env.get('APP_KEY'))),
          provider: AuthProvider(
            model: () => User(),
          ),
        ),
      },
    ));
  }
}

docs.title: 2. Register into dox app/config/services.dart
docs.text:
List<DoxService> services = <DoxService>[
  ... /// other services
  AuthService,
];

docs.title: 3. Register auth middleware
docs.text:
Register AuthMiddleware() in route.

Route.get('/auth/user', <dynamic>[
  AuthMiddleware(), 
  authController.user
]);

docs.title: 4. Attempt Login
docs.text:
Use auth package in controller to attempt login.

class AuthController {
    login() {
        Map<String, dynamic> credentials = req.only(<String>['email', 'password']);
        Auth auth = Auth();
        String? token = await auth.attempt(credentials);
        if(token != null) {
            User? user = auth.user<User>();
            return user;
        }
        return response("unauthorized").statusCode(401);
    }
}

docs.title: 5. Verify or Fetch User
docs.text:
Verify logged in user or fetch user information.

Future<dynamic> fetchUser(DoxRequest req) async {
  IAuth? auth = req.auth;
  if (auth?.isLoggedIn() == true) {
    return auth?.user();
  }
  throw UnAuthorizedException();
}

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
CORS, or Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, is a security feature implemented in web browsers to control and regulate requests made between web pages from different origins (domains). It ensures that web applications running at one domain are allowed or restricted from making requests to resources (such as data or services) hosted on a different domain. CORS helps prevent potentially harmful cross-site request forgery (CSRF) and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks while enabling safe data sharing and interaction between web applications on separate domains when configured appropriately.

CORS configuration can be found in lib/config/cors.dart

cors.dart 
CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
    /// Enabled
    /// -------------------------------
    /// A boolean to enable or disable CORS integration.
    /// Setting to true will enable the CORS for all HTTP request.
    enabled: true,

    /// Origin
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of allowed origins.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed origins.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request origins.
    origin: '*',

    /// Methods
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Request-Method`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of request methods.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of request methods.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request methods.
    methods: '*',

    /// Headers
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of allowed headers.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of allowed headers.
    /// String (*)  : A wildcard (*) to allow all request headers.
    headers: '*',

    /// Expose Headers
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Set a list of origins to be allowed for `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.
    /// The value can be one of the following:
    /// Array       : An array of expose headers.
    /// String      : Comma separated list of expose headers.
    exposeHeaders: <String>[
        'cache-control',
        'content-language',
        'content-type',
        'expires',
        'last-modified',
        'pragma',
    ],

    /// Credentials
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Toggle `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.
    credentials: true,

    /// MaxAge
    /// -------------------------------
    /// Define `Access-Control-Max-Age` header in seconds.
    maxAge: 90,
);

docs.title: Encode
docs.text:
String encodedMessage = AESEncryptor.encode('Hello world', 'your-secret');
print(encodedMessage);

docs.title: Controller
Parameters
docs.text:
A controller asks for what it needs by type. Dox fills each parameter.

Route.put('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', controller.update);

class UserController {
    Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
Parameter type Dox gives DoxRequest the request a @Dto class the checked body or query. See Validation. String, int, double, num, bool the path params, in the order of the route the same types with ? an optional path param ({id?}). null when it is not in the URL.

Rules:

  • The order of parameters is free. Path params are matched by position: the first path-param parameter gets the first {...} in the route.
  • DoxRequest is not needed. Add it only when you use it.
  • At most one @Dto parameter.
  • Only positional parameters. Named and [optional] parameters are not supported.
  • A catch-all {path*} param is a String.
  • The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.

Path param types. Text from the URL is converted:

  • int: "42" is 42. "abc" or "4.5" answers 404 Not Found: no such page.
  • double, num: "4.5" is 4.5.
  • bool: true, 1 / false, 0.
  • Any other text answers 404 too.
  • Path params are checked first. When one is wrong, the DTO is not checked.

Checked at start. The server does not start when:

  • a parameter type is not in the list above, and not a @Dto (did you run dart run build_runner build?),
  • the method has more path-param parameters than the route has {...} params.

Why types, not names?

Dox reads the parameter types of your method once, when the routes are registered at start. It needs no dart:mirrors. So update(int teamId, int id) works by position, not by the names teamId and id.

Typed input (recommended)
docs.text:
Ask for a DTO in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET), checks it, and gives you a typed object.

class ApiController {
    Future<String> sayHello(HelloInput input) async {
        return 'Hello ${input.name}';

}

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See Validation.

docs.title: Raw input
docs.text:
You can still read the raw values from the request. req.body['name'] and req.input('name') read the JSON body, the form data and the query string (?foo=bar). These values are not checked.

class ApiController {
    String sayHello(DoxRequest req) {
        String name = req.input('name');
        return 'Hello $name';
    }
}

docs.title: Route param
docs.text:
Ask for a path param as a typed parameter. int id gets 42 from /users/42.

Route.get('/hello/{name}', controller.sayHello);
Route.get('/users/{id}', controller.show);

class ApiController {
    String sayHello(String name) {
        return 'Hello $name';
    }

    Future<User?> show(int id) async {
        return User().find(id);
    }
}

The values are also in req.param. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. The request must be multipart/form-data. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
    @Image()
    @MaxSize('5MB')
    final RequestFile image;

    const UploadImage({required this.image});

    static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}

class ApiController {
    Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
        String uploadedPath = await input.image.store('images');
        return <String, String>{'filename': uploadedPath};
    }
}

Without a DTO, req.input('image') gives the RequestFile, not checked.

docs.title: RequestFile
docs.text:
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage. returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files

Save the file before you return

A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is streamed to a temp file while it arrives. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. So call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413 Payload Too Large. Dox checks Content-Length first, and also counts the bytes while reading.

AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);   // value as sent

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The response can take various forms, including strings, maps, models, serializers, lists of models, and various types of exceptions.

stringexceptionmap/jsonmodellist of modelfiledownloadstream 
/// string
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return 'pong';
    }
}

/// exception
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return InternalErrorException();
    }
}

/// map
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        return {"message" : "hello world!"};
    }
}

/// Model
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        Admin admin = await Admin().find(1)
        return admin;
    }
}

/// List<Model>
class BlogController {
    index(DoxRequest req) {
        List admins = await Admin().all()
        return admins;
    }
}

/// File: streamed, with Content-Length and Range support
class VideoController {
    show(DoxRequest req) {
        return File('storage/video.mp4');
    }
}

/// DownloadableFile
class PdfController {
    download(DoxRequest req) async {
        DownloadableFile file = await Storage().download('filename.pdf');

        return file;
    }
}

/// StreamFile
class PdfController {
    download(DoxRequest req) async {
        StreamFile file = await Storage().stream('filename.pdf');

        return file;
    }
}

Info

Models and lists of models will be automatically converted into JSON format and arrays of JSON.

docs.title: Files and big responses
docs.text:
Return a File or a Stream<List<int>>. Dox pipes it to the client. It does not load it all into memory.

  • A File sets Content-Type (from the file name), Content-Length and Accept-Ranges.
  • It answers Range: bytes=... with 206 Partial Content. Video players can seek, and downloads can resume.
  • Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file.
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

Validation rules
docs.text:
Every annotation you can put on a @Dto field. See Validation for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

  • Code is the error code. Use it in @Dto(messages: ...) and in a MessageResolver.
  • Message is the default English text. {field} is the last key of the path.
  • Every annotation also takes message:. It wins over every other message.
  • All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
  • On a List<T> field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

docs.title: Type errors
docs.text:
These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

Code When Message required a required field is missing, null, or "" The {field} is required string not a string The {field} must be a string integer not a whole number The {field} must be an integer numeric not a number (double, num) The {field} must be a number boolean not a bool The {field} must be a boolean date not an ISO 8601 date The {field} must be a date in not a name of the enum The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} array not a list The {field} must be an array object not an object (nested DTO, Map) The {field} must be an object file not a file The {field} must be a file unrecognized_keys unknown key, with @Dto(strict: true) The {field} field is not allowed

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
For String fields (and List<String> items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Length(min: 3, max: 50) length_between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters minLength, maxLength @Length(min: 6, max: 6) length The {field} must be exactly {length} characters minLength, maxLength @MinLength(3) min_length The {field} must be at least {min} characters minLength @MaxLength(50) max_length The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters maxLength @Email() email The {field} is not a valid email format: email @Url() url The {field} must be a url format: uri @Uuid() uuid The {field} is invalid uuid format: uuid @Ip() ip The {field} must be an ip address anyOf ipv4 / ipv6 @Regex(r'[a-z]+') regex The {field} format is invalid pattern @In(['a', 'b']) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn(['root']) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum} @StartsWith('dox') start_with The {field} must start with {prefix} pattern @EndsWith('.dev') end_with The {field} must end with {suffix} pattern @Alpha() alpha The {field} must be an alphabetic pattern @AlphaNumeric() alpha_numeric The {field} must be only alphabetic and number pattern @AlphaDash() alpha_dash The {field} must be only alphabetic and dash pattern

Details:

  • @Length has min: and max:. Both are optional, but you must give one. With only min: it acts like @MinLength, with only max: like @MaxLength.
  • Length counts characters (Unicode code points). é counts as 1.
  • @Url() needs http or https and a host.
  • @Uuid() takes any version. Upper or lower case.
  • @Regex(pattern, {message}) must match the whole value. You do not need ^ and $. The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
  • @Alpha(), @AlphaNumeric() and @AlphaDash() use ASCII letters a-z, A-Z. @AlphaDash() also allows - and _.
  • @In and @NotIn compare exactly (case matters).

docs.title: Change text
docs.text:
These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them: @Trim, then @Lowercase or @Uppercase, then the "empty string is missing" check.

Annotation Does @Trim() removes spaces at the start and the end @Lowercase() makes the text lower case @Uppercase() makes the text upper case @AllowEmpty() keeps "" as a value. Without it, "" counts as missing.

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. @Lowercase() and @Uppercase() together stop the build.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
For int, double and num fields (and list items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Min(18) min The {field} must be greater than or equal {min} minimum @Max(100) max The {field} must be less than or equal {max} maximum @Range(1, 10) between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} minimum, maximum @Positive() greater_than The {field} must be greater than 0 exclusiveMinimum: 0 @GreaterThan(0.5) greater_than The {field} must be greater than {min} (exclusive) exclusiveMinimum @LessThan(100) less_than The {field} must be less than {max} (exclusive) exclusiveMaximum @In([1, 2, 3]) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn([0]) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum}

The values are num. @Min(1.5) on an int field stops the build.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
For List<T> fields. These check the list, not the items.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MinItems(1) min_items The {field} must have at least {min} items minItems @MaxItems(5) max_items The {field} may not have more than {max} items maxItems @UniqueItems() unique_items The {field} must not have duplicate items uniqueItems: true

@UniqueItems() works for String, numbers, bool, enums and DateTime. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

docs.title: Dates
docs.text:
For DateTime fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @After('2000-01-01') after The {field} must be a date after {date} format: date-time @Before('now') before The {field} must be a date before {date} format: date-time
  • The value is an ISO 8601 date, or 'now' (the time of the request).
  • Both are exclusive: @After('2000-01-01') does not accept 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
  • To compare two fields (end after start), use validate().

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
For RequestFile and List<RequestFile> fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MaxSize('2MB') max_size The {field} may not be larger than {max} maxLength (bytes) @Mimes(['pdf', 'png']) mimes The {field} must be a file of type: {types} contentMediaType @Image() image The {field} must be an image contentMediaType: image/*
  • @MaxSize units: B, KB, MB, GB. 1KB = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
  • @Mimes takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file. For types without a byte signature (like txt or csv), it uses the file name extension.
  • @Image() is @Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp']). No svg.
  • The JSON Schema of a file is {"type": "string", "format": "binary"}, plus the keys above.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
From dox_orm. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

Annotation Code Message @Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection}) unique The {field} has already been taken @Exists(table, {column, connection}) exists The selected {field} is invalid
  • @Unique column default: the input key. @Exists column default: id.
  • ignoreParam: 'id' skips the row where ignoreColumn (default id) equals the path param {id}.
  • They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See Database rules.

docs.title: Keys and DTO options
docs.text:
Annotation Does @Name('emailAddress') the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. @Dto() marks the class. @Dto(source: Source.query) where to read: Source.auto (default), Source.query, Source.body. @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) keys: KeyCase.snake (default) or KeyCase.field (the Dart name as is). @Dto(strict: true) unknown keys are errors. Default false: they are dropped. @Dto(messages: {...}) messages by code or key.code.

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: What the generator checks
docs.text:
The build stops with a clear error when:

  • a field is not final, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
  • a field type is not supported (see Types),
  • a rule does not fit the field type (like @Email() on an int),
  • a Maybe<T> field has no const Maybe.missing() default,
  • two @Dto classes in the app have the same name,
  • the class is generic, or extends another class (other than Object).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Write a class with @Dto(). Ask for it in your controller. Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object. When the input is wrong, Dox answers 422 with the errors. Your controller does not run.

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

enum Role { admin, user }

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable = optional

  final Role role; // must be "admin" or "user"

  @MaxItems(5)
  final List<String> tags;

  const CreateUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    this.age,
    this.role = Role.user,
    this.tags = const <String>[],
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked. body.age is an int?, body.role is a Role.
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}

Then run the generator:

dart run build_runner build

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You do this once per app.

  1. Put DTOs in lib/app/http/dtos/. Name the file <name>.dto.dart. dox create:dto CreateUser makes lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart for you.
  2. Each DTO file has part '<name>.dto.g.dart'; and the schema line: static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
  3. Run dart run build_runner build (or dox build_runner:watch). It writes a .dto.g.dart file next to each DTO and one list of all DTOs in lib/dtos.g.dart.
  4. Give that list to the app in lib/config/app.dart:
import 'package:my_app/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);

Why the list?

Dox does not use dart:mirrors. So it can not find a class by its name at runtime. The generated list tells Dox which classes are DTOs. You never edit it by hand.

What the generator makes for each DTO (no reflection, works with dox build AOT):

  • the checks for every field,
  • the code that turns the input map into your class,
  • a JSON Schema, used by the OpenAPI docs.

docs.title: As a controller parameter
docs.text:
Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with path params and the request
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

See Controller: parameters for the full rules.

docs.title: Inside a method
docs.text:
req.validate<T>() does the same work. It returns the object or throws the 422 error.

Future<User> store(DoxRequest req) async {
  CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
  // ...
}

req.validate<T>() is always async. Always await it.

docs.title: Required and optional
docs.text:
The Dart type decides. You do not write required or nullable.

Field Missing key null Result final String name; (no default) error required error required required final int? age; null null optional final Role role; with this.role = Role.user the default error required optional, has a default final Maybe<String?> bio; with this.bio = const Maybe.missing() isPresent == false isPresent == true, value == null optional, knows "missing" from null

Rules:

  • Required = not nullable and no default in the constructor.
  • Optional = nullable (T?), or has a default.
  • A default is used only when the key is missing. A default value is not checked by the rules.
  • null is never allowed for a non-nullable field, even when it has a default.
  • An empty string counts as missing. After @Trim(), "" is treated like a missing key, in JSON, query and form data. So a required String rejects "" and " " (with @Trim()). A String? gets null. Add @AllowEmpty() to keep "" as a real value.
  • Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.

docs.title: Missing or null? (for PATCH)
docs.text:
A T? field gives null for both a missing key and a null value. When you must know the difference, use Maybe<T>. Its default must be const Maybe.missing().

@Dto()
class UpdateUser {
  @Length(max: 500)
  final Maybe<String?> bio;

  const UpdateUser({this.bio = const Maybe.missing()});

  static const DtoSchema<UpdateUser> schema = $UpdateUserDto;
}

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}

Rules on a Maybe<T> field check value when it is present and not null.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Dart type JSON Query and form data (text) String a string as is int a whole number (18 or 18.0) "18" double any number (18 becomes 18.0) "4.5", "18" num any number "18", "4.5" bool true / false true, 1, yes, on / false, 0, no, off (any case) DateTime an ISO 8601 string the same an enum the name, like "admin" the same RequestFile not allowed a file part in multipart/form-data a @Dto class an object bracket keys, like address[city] List<T> an array repeated keys tags=a&tags=b, or tags[]=a&tags[]=b Map<String, T> an object with any keys bracket keys, like meta[color] Object?, dynamic, Map<String, dynamic> any JSON, not checked any text, not checked

JSON is strict. In a JSON body, "18" is not an int. You get the error integer. Query and form data are text, so Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error (like integer or boolean).

More details:

  • int never takes a fraction. "4.5" or 4.5 gives the error integer.
  • DateTime takes 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31T10:00:00Z. A value without a time zone is read as UTC. The result is always UTC (isUtc == true). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
  • An enum matches the name exactly. "Admin" does not match Role.admin.
  • In query and form data, one value for a List<T> field gives a list with one item.
  • In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: items[3] alone gives a list with one item. A list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives 422.
  • The generator stops with an error for any other type.

docs.title: Where the data comes from
docs.text:
Request Dox reads GET, HEAD, DELETE the query string POST, PUT, PATCH the body

Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body. So a query value can not overwrite a body value.

The body can be:

  • JSON: application/json (or any +json type). Strict types.
  • application/x-www-form-urlencoded: text, converted.
  • multipart/form-data: text, converted. Files go to RequestFile fields.

Other content types get 415 Unsupported Media Type. A body that is not valid JSON gets 400 Bad Request. A JSON body that is not an object (like [1, 2]) gets 422 with the key _root.

docs.title: Choose the source
docs.text:
Set it on the DTO, when this DTO is always read from one place:

@Dto(source: Source.query) // also for POST
class SearchUsers { ... }

Or set it for one call:

SearchUsers filter = await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query);

Source.auto (the default) uses the table above. Source.query and Source.body force one source.

docs.title: Path params
docs.text:
Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as typed controller parameters:

Route.put('/users/{id}', controller.update);

Future<User> update(int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

A path param that does not fit its type (like abc for int id) answers 404. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Keys: snake_case by default
docs.text:
The JSON key is the field name in snake_case, the same as the ORM. firstName reads first_name.

@Dto()
class SignUp {
  final String firstName; // key: first_name

  @Name('emailAddress')
  final String email; // key: emailAddress

  const SignUp({required this.firstName, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}

To use the field names as they are (camelCase), set it on the DTO:

@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) // firstName reads firstName

Error keys always use the input key (first_name), not the Dart name.

docs.title: Unknown keys
docs.text:
Keys that the DTO does not have are dropped. You never see them.

With @Dto(strict: true), an unknown key is an error:

{ "is_admin": "The is_admin field is not allowed" }

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Put rules on a field as annotations. A field can have many. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error for that field.

@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;

Every rule is in the rules reference. The short list:

Kind Annotations Text @Length, @MinLength, @MaxLength, @Email, @Url, @Uuid, @Ip, @Regex, @In, @NotIn, @StartsWith, @EndsWith, @Alpha, @AlphaNumeric, @AlphaDash Change text @Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase, @AllowEmpty Numbers @Min, @Max, @Range, @Positive, @GreaterThan, @LessThan, @In, @NotIn Lists @MinItems, @MaxItems, @UniqueItems Dates @After, @Before Files @MaxSize, @Mimes, @Image Database @Unique, @Exists (from dox_orm) Keys @Name

Rules on a list check each item

@Email() on a List<String> checks every item. The error key is emails.2. Only @MinItems, @MaxItems and @UniqueItems check the list itself.

The generator stops with an error when a rule does not fit the type, like @Email() on an int.

Name clash

dox_core exports the rule names (Uuid, Name, Range, Image, ...). A file that also imports a package with the same name, like package:uuid, gets an "ambiguous import" error. Fix it with hide: import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;. dox_orm has a Schema class too: import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;.

docs.title: Enums or @In
docs.text:
Use a Dart enum when you can. The allowed values are the enum names. Use @In([...]) for a plain String or int with a few allowed values:

final Role role;              // "admin" or "user"

@In(<String>['draft', 'published'])
final String status;

docs.title: Nested objects and lists
docs.text:
A field can be another @Dto class, or a list of them.

@Dto()
class Address {
  final String city;

  @Length(min: 5, max: 5)
  final String postCode;

  const Address({required this.city, required this.postCode});

  static const DtoSchema<Address> schema = $AddressDto;
}

@Dto()
class OrderItem {
  final String name;

  @Positive()
  final int quantity;

  const OrderItem({required this.name, required this.quantity});

  static const DtoSchema<OrderItem> schema = $OrderItemDto;
}

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}

{
  "address": { "city": "Bangkok", "post_code": "10110" },
  "items": [
    { "name": "Shoes", "quantity": 2 },
    { "name": "Socks", "quantity": 0 }
  ]
}

Error: {"items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"}.

A nested DTO has its own options (keyCase, strict). A nullable nested field (Address?) is optional.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A RequestFile field reads a file from multipart/form-data.

@Dto()
class UploadAvatar {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('2MB')
  final RequestFile avatar;

  @MaxItems(5)
  @Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
  final List<RequestFile> documents; // documents[] or repeated documents

  const UploadAvatar({required this.avatar, this.documents = const <RequestFile>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadAvatar> schema = $UploadAvatarDto;
}
  • Dox reads the first bytes of the file to find its real type. The file name and the client content type are not trusted.
  • @Image() allows jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp and bmp. Not svg, because an SVG can hold scripts.
  • A text field sent where a file is expected gives the error file.
  • Save the file before you return. See Request: form data.

docs.title: Checks across fields: validate()
docs.text:
Add a method validate(DtoErrors errors) to the DTO. Dox calls it after every field rule passed. At that point, all fields have their typed values.

@Dto()
class SignUp {
  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  final String passwordConfirmation;

  final DateTime? startsAt;
  final DateTime? endsAt;

  const SignUp({
    required this.password,
    required this.passwordConfirmation,
    this.startsAt,
    this.endsAt,
  });

  void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
    if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
      errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
    }
    if (startsAt != null && endsAt != null && !endsAt!.isAfter(startsAt!)) {
      errors.add('ends_at', 'The end must be after the start');
    }
  }

  static const DtoSchema<SignUp> schema = $SignUpDto;
}

The exact API:

  • The method is named validate. It takes one DtoErrors and returns void or Future<void>.
  • errors.add(String key, String message) adds an error. key is the input key (snake_case), not the Dart name. The message is used as it is (no placeholders, no message resolver).
  • errors.has(String key) is true when that key already has an error.
  • Use the key _root for an error that is not about one field.
  • In a nested DTO, keys are relative. Dox adds the parent path: address.post_code.
  • Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

docs.title: Database rules: @Unique and @Exists
docs.text:
These come from dox_orm. They read the database, so they run last.

import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
  final int teamId;

  @Exists('tags')
  final List<int> tagIds; // checks every item in one query

  const CreateUser({required this.email, required this.teamId, this.tagIds = const <int>[]});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
Annotation Passes when @Unique(table, {column}) no row has this value. column defaults to the input key. @Exists(table, {column}) a row has this value. column defaults to id.

For an update, skip the row you are updating. ignoreParam names a path param:

// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id') // WHERE id != {id}
final String email;
  • ignoreColumn: sets the id column. Default id.
  • connection: uses another dox_orm connection. Default: the default connection.
  • Soft-deleted rows count too.
  • Upper or lower case: this depends on your database collation.
  • On a List<T> field, each item is checked. All items use one WHERE IN query.

docs.title: The order of checks
docs.text:
1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (@Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase). Missing required fields.
  2. The field rules, top to bottom.
  3. The validate() method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
  4. Async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

  • Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. A nested DTO checks its own types first, then its own rules. So one answer can have a type error in address and a rule error in items.1.
  • Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
  • A default value is not checked by the field rules. (Async rules check the final value.)

docs.title: The error response
docs.text:
When a check fails, Dox answers 422 Unprocessable Entity with a flat JSON object. The key is the path to the value. The value is one message (the first error of that field).

{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "address.city": "The city is required",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
  • Paths use dots. List items use the index: tags.0.
  • Paths use the input keys (post_code), after @Name and keyCase.
  • _root is for errors about the whole body.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Every rule has a default English message. See the rules reference.

Placeholders: {field} is the last key of the path (for list items: the list key). {value} is the input value. Rules add their own, like {min} and {max}.

docs.title: On one rule
docs.text:
Every annotation takes message:.

@Email(message: 'Please check your email')
@Length(min: 3, message: 'At least {min} letters, please')

docs.title: On one DTO
docs.text:
@Dto(messages: ...) sets messages by code, or by key.code. Use it for messages that have no annotation, like required or a type error.

@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})

docs.title: For the whole app, and other languages
docs.text:
Dox finds a message in this order:

  1. message: on the annotation.
  2. @Dto(messages:): first key.code (like email.required), then code.
  3. The app message resolver.
  4. The default English text.

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and set it in the config. request.locale is the first language in the Accept-Language header, like th. It is null when there is none.

class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code];
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);

MessageRequest has code, path, params, fallback, customMessage and locale.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
A rule is a class that extends Rule<T>. It needs a const constructor, so you can use it as an annotation. T is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

@Dto()
class CreatePost {
  @Slug()
  final String slug;

  const CreatePost({required this.slug});

  static const DtoSchema<CreatePost> schema = $CreatePostDto;
}
  • A rule with values: add final fields and override params. They become placeholders.
  • RuleContext gives path, field, root (the whole input) and lookup('other.key').
  • Override toJsonSchema() to add JSON Schema keys, like {'pattern': '^[a-z0-9-]+$'}.
  • A check that needs the database: extend AsyncRule<T> and implement Future<bool> checkAsync(T value, RuleContext context). It runs in step 4 of the order of checks.
class MinValue extends Rule<int> {
  const MinValue(this.min, {super.message});

  final int min;

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'min_value';
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be at least {min}';
  }

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> get params {
    return <String, Object?>{'min': min};
  }

  @override
  bool check(int value, RuleContext context) {
    return value >= min;
  }
}

docs.title: Dynamic input: fluent schemas
docs.text:
Some input has a shape you only know at runtime, like custom form fields from the database. For that, build a schema with v.object(...) and use req.validateSchema(). It returns a Map.

Map<String, Schema<Object?>> fields = <String, Schema<Object?>>{};
for (FormField f in form.fields) {
  fields[f.key] = f.required ? v.string().min(1) : v.string().optional();
}

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));

Use a DTO for everything else. See dox_validation.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Make a DTO directly. It is a normal Dart class. This skips all checks.

CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');
await userService.create(input);

Check a map with the rules, like a request would:

CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'Ann',
  'email': 'ann@dox.dev',
});
expect(user.role, Role.user);

Check the errors with safeValidateMap. It never throws.

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors, <String, String>{
  'name': 'The name must be between 3 and 50 characters',
  'email': 'The email is not a valid email',
});

Options of both methods:

  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string (text is converted). Default: Source.body with JSON types.
  • params: {'id': '5'} gives path params, for @Unique(ignoreParam: 'id').

@Unique and @Exists need a database. Use a test database, or test those fields in an integration test.

docs.title: Not in 3.0
docs.text:
• A DTO can not extend another class, and can not be generic. The generator stops with an error.
  • An enum value is always its Dart name. Custom wire values (like "ADMIN" for Role.admin) are not supported.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• The generator writes plain Dart code for each DTO. No reflection, no rule strings to parse.
  • A check is a few if statements per field. Regexes are compiled once.
  • Dox finds the DTO for a route once, then keeps it.
  • It works with dox build (AOT).
